event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: KO’s 2023-02-21 filing contains a concentrated, up-to-date discussion of COVID-19 as both a realised and continuing enterprise-wide threat.  Multiple sentences (1) acknowledge concrete, already-incurred impacts – lower sales, shifts to at-home consumption and global supply-chain breakdowns – and (2) emphasise that those effects could intensify or re-emerge if infection rates rise.  The narrative is recent (within three years of the pandemic declaration), uses strong, materiality-charged language (e.g., “material adverse effect,” “negatively impacted”) and specifies several operating vectors: consumer-demand migration, input shortages, plant closures, logistics delays and cost inflation.  While a few sentences note partial recovery, no material mitigating actions or quantified offsets are offered.  Under the Time Decay Principle, COVID-19 sits in the 0-3-year window, so evidence can receive high severity scores.  Because the disclosures combine concrete historical damage with forward-looking uncertainty across critical functions, the overall risk profile is assessed as high to very high, warranting snippet scores generally in the 6-8 range.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and related ongoing impacts may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

components.reason: Uses strong materiality wording ('material adverse effect').
Directly ties risk to COVID-19 pandemic, a recent event.
Forward-looking, indicating the threat is still live within 0-3-year window.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: High-impact terminology and explicit link to the recent pandemic yield a solid severity score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: Since early 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic and the related actions by governments around the world to attempt to contain the spread of the virus have negatively impacted, and could continue to negatively impact, our business globally.

components.reason: Confirms actual historical negative impacts to the business.
States possibility of continued future harm.
Covers global scope, amplifying breadth of risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Combination of realised damage and ongoing global exposure supports a high risk score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: At times we have experienced a decrease in sales of certain of our products in markets around the world, as well as a shift in consumer demand to more at-home consumption versus away-from-home consumption.

components.reason: Details concrete operational impact: decreased sales.
Highlights fundamental shift in consumer demand patterns.
Impacts span multiple global markets.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific, worldwide revenue and demand effects justify a strong score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: While we have experienced improved trends throughout 2021 and 2022 in away-from-home channels and improved margins, our recovery has been asynchronous, and the full extent to which the COVID-19 pandemic will affect our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows will depend on future developments that are highly uncertain.

components.reason: Admits recovery remains uneven ('asynchronous').
Emphasises high future uncertainty over financial impacts.
Mentions some improvement, a partial mitigating element.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Uncertainty and incomplete recovery raise risk, but noted improvements temper severity, netting a moderate score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: If COVID-19 infection rates increase, the pandemic intensifies, or continued efforts to curb the pandemic are ineffective, the negative impacts of the pandemic on our sales could be more prolonged and may become more severe than what we have experienced to date.

components.reason: Warns of potential for prolonged and more severe sales impacts.
Scenario-based escalation underscores forward-looking vulnerability.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Future-escalation language without mitigation drives a moderate-high score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted and could continue to disrupt our global supply chain.

components.reason: Explicitly states supply-chain disruption, a core operational risk.
Continued disruption expected (forward-looking).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct mention of ongoing global supply-chain disruption warrants a high score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: We and our bottling partners have experienced temporary disruptions in certain of our operations; delays in delivery of concentrates, ingredients, packaging and equipment; temporary plant closures; production slowdowns; and difficulty or delays in sourcing key ingredients and beverage containers.

components.reason: Lists multiple concrete operational breakdowns already experienced.
Covers critical inputs and production capacity, heightening severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed catalogue of realised supply-chain and production issues drives a 6-point severity assessment.

evidence_list.snippet: We and our bottling partners may face similar disruptions in the future, which may increase supply chain and packaging costs, or may result in an inability to secure key ingredients and inputs, which could cause delays in delivering our products to our customers and consumers.

components.reason: Projects future recurrence of disruptions, extending risk horizon.
Highlights cost inflation and delivery delays – material financial and operational impacts.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking cost and delivery threats keep risk significant, producing a 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Although we are unable to predict the impact on our ability to source materials in the future, we expect supply chain pressures to continue into 2023.

components.reason: Acknowledges inability to forecast sourcing impact, signalling uncertainty.
Confirms expectation of ongoing supply pressures into the next fiscal year.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Explicit expectation of continued supply strain adds moderate severity (score 4).

evidence_list.snippet: In addition to the above risks, the COVID-19 pandemic may exacerbate other risks related to our business, including risks related to changes in the retail landscape or the loss of key retail or foodservice customers; fluctuations in input costs, inflation rates, and foreign currency exchange rates; and the ability of third-party service providers and business partners to fulfill their respective commitments and responsibilities to us in a timely manner and in accordance with the agreed-upon terms.

components.reason: Shows pandemic as a multiplier, worsening several other strategic risks.
Mentions broad operational areas (customers, costs, partners).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Risk-amplification across multiple domains yields a solid score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: The continuing evolution of the pandemic may also present risks not currently known to us.

components.reason: States existence of unknown, potentially emergent risks.
Highlights ongoing uncertainty and limits of risk visibility.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but important uncertainty acknowledgement merits a modest score of 3.
